findings.title: updateMany with empty data will throw
findings.body: fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache calls SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {}) with empty data. Prisma rejects updateMany when data is empty (Invalid invocation: data must not be empty), so every cache warm-up will now throw after writing the cache. Pass an explicit field like { updatedAt: new Date() } or remove the call.

findings.title: Delete-cache success never invalidates cache status query
findings.body: deleteCacheMutation onSuccess only shows a toast and calls onSuccess?.(), while disconnectMutation invalidates viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars and viewer.apps.integrations onSettled. After deleting cached data the connectedCalendars query still holds the old cacheUpdatedAt, so the dropdown keeps showing a stale Last updated timestamp until a manual refetch.

findings.title: Cache status ignores expiry, shows stale cache
findings.body: getCacheStatusByCredentialIds groups all CalendarCache rows by credentialId with no expiresAt filter, while getCachedAvailability only honors rows with expiresAt >= now. A credential whose rows are all expired will still report an updatedAt and the UI will offer Delete cached data for unusable cache.

findings.title: macOS-only sed breaks script on Linux
findings.body: The script uses sed -i '' -E to rewrite GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL. The empty backup-suffix argument is BSD/macOS syntax; on GNU/Linux sed it is parsed as an input file and fails, so the helper cannot update the env file on Linux/CI containers. Use a portable update or detect OS.

findings.title: Auth failure throws generic Error instead of TRPCError
findings.body: When the credential is not found or belongs to another user the handler throws new Error("Credential not found or access denied"). Other viewer routers use TRPCError with NOT_FOUND/FORBIDDEN codes, so clients cannot distinguish auth failure from an internal error and get a 500 instead of a coded error.
